etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Compound of 御(お) (o-, beautifying prefix) + しまい (shimai, “ending, finishing”, 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb しまう (shimau, “to finish, to end”)).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/kaku/ → /kau/ → /kɔː/ → /koː/
Shift from 斯(か)く (kaku).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: The perfective form of しまう (shimau, “to finish”), literally meaning “finished”. Compare Mandarin 完了 (wánle).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From English cup. Doublet (via Late Latin cuppa) of コップ (koppu), from Dutch kop and Portuguese copo.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
Middle Chinese 交叉
差 is a daiyōji replacing 叉.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Chinese 會館 /会馆 (huìguǎn). Analyzable as 会 (kai, “meeting; gathering”) + 館 (kan, “public building”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 受話(じゅわ) (juwa, “listening on a telephone”) + 器(き) (-ki, “device”)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Borrowed from Middle Chinese 同僚 (MC duwng lew).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Shift from 向(む)き合(あ)う (mukiau).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 善 (MC dzyenX).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: ささ (sasa, an onomatopoeia) + やく (-yaku, a verb-forming suffix attaching to mimetic words)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 字 (MC dziH).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Old Japanese. First attested in the Nihon Shoki of 720 CE.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Shortened form of azana above.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 寒 (“cold”) + 帯 (“belt”)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Old Japanese 寝 (nu).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Sound shift from ひきかかる (hikikakaru).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Adjectivization of verb 恐(おそ)る (osoru, “to fear”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese compound 摩擦 (MC ma tshat).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From the -te conjunctive form of verb 改める (aratameru).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 段 (MC dwanH).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Classical terminal form of the modern adjective 無(な)い (nai).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 真っ (ma'-, “truly”) + 先 (saki, “first”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
First cited to the mid-800s.
From 膨, 脹 (fukura, “a bulge, a swelling”) + む (-mu, suffix indicating “looks like, seems like”). The fukura portion is in turn from now-archaic verb 膨る, 脹る (fukuru, “to swell, to bulge”), superseded by modern 膨れる, 脹れる (fukureru) of the same meaning.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Cognate with 粗(あら)い (arai).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: The 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 誇(ほこ)る (hokoru, “to be proud of”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Cognate with Japanese 乗(の)る (noru).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 追(お)う (ou, “to chase”) + 越(こ)す (kosu, “to go past”)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 道 (michi, “way”) + 順 (jun, “order”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 避(さ)く (saku), cognate with Japanese 裂ける (sakeru). See the page for 避(さ)く (saku) for more information.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 部首 (MC buX syuwX). First mentioned in Chinese in the Shūowén Jiězì of roughly 100 CE.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Likely the same word as 汲(く)む (kumu, “to pour”) and 斟(く)む (kumu, “to consider people's feelings”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Old Japanese. Compare 嵩(かさ)む (kasamu, “to increase”), かさ張(ば)る (kasabaru, “to grow bulky”).
